violated_contract: A transport send is not server confirmation. A live capture surface that marks frames synced at socket-send time and skips durable storage for all-synced chunks holds no local copy of the audio it already handed off, so the end-of-session transcript confirmation has no stamped copy to judge or repair, and the retry budget of a transient failure class ends with the process instead of the network epoch. The same contract covers composer input: a draft cleared before the send is acknowledged has no restorable copy.
canonical_prevention: Keep a durable local safety copy for every live frame until the server confirms it: the phone-mic buffer stores chunks exactly like the Apple Watch safety copy (a transport send never starts the retention clock - syncedAt stays 0), the lifecycle pause seals and flushes the in-memory tail the way the Watch checkpoint does, the conversation stamp binds transport-only synced copies so confirmSessionTranscription can release covered copies into synced retention and reclassify uncovered ones for repair upload, a cold start re-arms the transient retry budget exactly like a connectivity restore (durable HTTP refusals keep their persisted clock), and the chat composer persists its draft and clears it only after the send is accepted.
